newsitem.title: UK: Strong stg hits UK grain futures, Egypt helps.
newsitem.headline: Strong stg hits UK grain futures, Egypt helps.

text.p: LIFFE grain futures fell as sterling's jump against continental currencies eroded UK grains' competitive position.

Egypt's purchase of 450,000 tonnes of French wheat on Sunday gave the market a steady start, but then sterling, as so often, came to dominate and pushed prices down. However, later in the day the market found underlying bids as prices came down, traders said.
Active May wheat last traded 0.30 stg lower at 96.20 stg, having seen a low of 96.00 stg. Volume for May was 170 lots, of a total 360 lots of wheat.
Sterling rose sharply amid heavy fund buying on sterling/mark and sterling/French franc, the two currencies UK domestic grain traders watch most carefully.
Egypt's main commodities buyer said on Sunday he bought a total 450,000 tonnes of French wheat for delivery in February, March and April at prices ranging between $140.70 and $143.90 FOB per tonne.
Samir Shakankiri, vice-chairman of the General Authority for Supply Commodities, said he bought the wheat in nine lots of 50,000 tonnes each.
Then on Monday he said he bought a further 50,000 tonnes of soft red French wheat for $140.50 per tonne for delivery between April 1 and April 31.
